title: Halifax DT524 Memorial, Wressle (Intake Plantation)
location_name: Intake Plantation (formerly Newsholme Plantation), Wressle, East Riding of Yorkshire, England
memorial_details: A plaque in Intake Plantation (formerly Newsholme Plantation), Wressle, marks the actual DT524 crash site. Metal-detector survey by local historians Albert Pritchard, Eric Barton, and Ken Reast confirmed DT524 wreckage at this woodland edge. Note: the plaque is sometimes understood locally as marking a JD151 memorial — this is a labelling or data error. The JD151 crash occurred approximately two miles away near Bowthorpe Hall, South Duffield. The plaque is on private land with no public right of way.
crew_summary: All ten killed — the largest single-incident death toll of the two crashes associated with this woodland site.
narrative:
DT524 took off from RAF Riccall at 10:05 on 7 September 1943 carrying a mixed crew of trainees working up to operational standard and three instructors. F/O Maynard Meyer Caplan DFM — a decorated pilot posted to instructional duties after completing his tour — was the senior crew member.

The exercise involved a Hurricane making simulated attacking passes while the Halifax crew practised evasive action under instructor direction. During the exercise the aircraft entered a spin. The starboard outer engine broke away from the wing and the aircraft dived into the ground at the edge of Newsholme Plantation (now Intake Plantation) near Wressle at around midday. All ten men aboard were killed.

Caplan had survived a full operational tour to earn his DFM, then was killed on a routine training flight within weeks of completing it. The mixed RAF and RCAF composition of the crew was typical of HCU operations, where Commonwealth aircrew trained together before joining operational squadrons.

One of the ten crew names has not been recovered from open sources.

Research by local historians Albert Pritchard, Eric Barton, and Ken Reast confirmed DT524 wreckage at the Intake Plantation site and established the two-mile separation from the JD151 crash near Bowthorpe Hall.

crew.name: Maynard Meyer Caplan
crew.fate_detail: Killed in training accident. Had been awarded DFM after completing operational tour.
